720	A few years ago, a young teacher in Jerusalem walked in
721	on his older teacher, who had taught him 40 years earlier.
722	The older teacher, already retired, sits at home, studies
723	the Daf Yomi class, another class, enjoying
724	the dividends, the fruits he once made grow. That
725	teacher walks into his home, sits down for a cup of
726	coffee and says to him, "Rabbi, listen, I studied
727	with you 40 years ago, I want you to know that thanks to you
728	I became a teacher. Because of a man like you, I chose the teaching
729	profession. It's not an easy profession, it's not a
730	rewarding one, certainly not in proportion to the effort. It's a profession full of
731	tension and full of disappointments. Even so, I chose this
732	hard profession because of people like you." The older teacher
733	smiles and says, "Tell me, I don't remember, I
734	barely remember that you studied with me. What happened?" He says to him,
735	"Listen, 40 years ago we were children, nine years old,
736	little kids. One morning a boy comes in with
737	a shiny watch. His father, a rich man, came back
738	from America and brought New York home. What was
739	bringing New York home? Buying a watch,
740	an electronic watch, the latest thing, some Casio
741	or I don't know what, on his wrist. And the children
742	around him, all of us poor kids, stroked
743	the watch, touched his hand, not believing it, from abroad,
744	on his wrist. At recess he put the watch
745	down somewhere, went off with the others to wash hands for bread,
746	and the watch disappeared. One of us stole it. The boy started
747	to shout, to scream: it's a gift from Dad, it's his honor,
748	it's his pride, you are thieves. The teacher came in
749	at the end of recess, heard what happened, that he had to set
750	things right. He stood all of us against the wall. We were little
751	children, nine years old. He told everyone to close their
752	eyes and raise their hands up. And he walked
753	among all of us. He reached me, put a hand in my pocket. The watch was there, I stole
754	it.
755	You said nothing. Everyone's eyes were closed. Not one
756	knew who it was. You returned it to that boy.
757	You said to him, 'There was a boy here whose evil inclination overcame
758	him. And now he regrets it and is returning
759	the watch to you.' And that was it. In that moment I said
760	to myself, if there are teachers like you in the world, who spared
761	me the shame, who said it was only the evil
762	inclination and not me, I decided in that moment that if a day
763	comes and the Holy One, Blessed Be He, gives me the means,
764	I will be a teacher myself. Then that boy says
765	to the older teacher, 'But one question has remained with me all these years,
766	I have been carrying it, for 40 years I have walked with this
767	question. Fine, you didn't shame me in front of my friends,
768	because you are a mensch. But how is it that you told me nothing?
769	How is it that you didn't call me after class and didn't give
770	me a moral rebuke? Kids like you end up in prison.
771	How is it that you didn't call my parents after class
772	to the principal's office and tell them, understand what kind of
773	twisted soul you are raising here, stop him early,
774	give him lessons in ethics, lessons in Chassidus? How is it
775	that you told me nothing, quietly?'"
776	The older teacher says, "Believe me, until this moment
777	I did not know that you were the thief, because I too searched
778	among you with my eyes closed."
779	Judging favorably is not lying, it is not saying
780	"He isn't a thief, he is looking for attention because his father is not
781	home." Judging favorably means believing that there is
782	more in a person than the evil within him.
783	There is good in a person alongside the evil in him. There is evil in him,
784	he has problems, he stole, but that is not the whole person.
785	"Judge the whole person favorably." What is the whole
786	person? The entire personality of the person, the totality
787	of the person. Because every person is a compound of darkness
788	and a compound of light. A compound of problem
789	and a compound of beauty. And whoever doesn't believe it, let him look at
790	himself. It is written in the Torah, "Love your neighbor as yourself." Each one
791	asks himself, what is "as yourself"? I can't manage to love myself. How
792	do I love others? And even if a person manages to love his wife and his children, today we don't manage. So many people
793	are frustrated. So you want me to love
794	the other, he is a stranger like myself. What is the meaning of this?
795	There is an explanation written by the grandson of the Alter Rebe, of
796	the Baal HaTanya, the Admor the Tzemach Tzedek. He says,
797	"Wonderful, powerful: 'Love your neighbor as yourself.' Judge
798	the other as you want to be judged.
799	When you sin and everyone is angry at you, you hurt
800	your wife and she is angry at you. What do you think to yourself?
801	You lie in bed, you see yourself?
802	So what do you say to yourself? Why does she forget
803	yesterday and the day before? Why does she remember only
804	this moment? Why doesn't she look at the whole,
805	at all the beauty in me? At all the lovely moments
806	that I devoted so much to her? We want them not
807	to remember only the evil in us, but to see the whole
808	person, the complete totality of the person, who is a divine
809	soul, 'in the image of Elokim He created man.' If you
810	believe that the world has a Creator, you must also believe
811	that every person is holy. 'Go tell the craftsman who made me,'
812	said that ugly man to Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon. 'The craftsman
813	who made me is beautiful,' so in every person there must be
814	beauty. Judge the whole person favorably: the meaning
815	is, believe that this person will have a chance, believe
816	that in this person you can still squeeze the lemon
817	and bring out the good in him. I say it like this:
818	judging the whole person favorably is not about what
819	was; what was was, it shouldn't have been; it's not about imagining
820	and creating a utopian reality. Something bad happened. To judge
821	favorably is about what will be, what can be.
822	The meaning is that I know that although this person
823	stole from me and hurt me, he has a divine soul.
824	He is a divine creation. He is a creation of the Holy One,
825	Blessed Be He. And the instruction of Yehoshua ben Perachia:
826	try to approach the good in him. In any case, do not
827	despair. Try to squeeze the lemon and see the
828	good in it. And so approach him. And what does this mean?
829	It means something very simple, and this is what I want to
830	get to in the class. Judge the person favorably.
831	The meaning is... I want to draw from this a very, very simple tip
832	that I try very, very hard to follow. It is
833	very hard. But there was not a single time that I tried
834	and it didn't succeed and I didn't see blessing from it.
